clue.text: Safeguard for example, aluminium going back in plane's body

parts.note: a fuse is a safety device that protects a circuit

indicators.note: going back says the two short pieces just before it are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Talk of protecting aircraft, perhaps with metal returned to the airframe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' reverses the example abbreviation and the metal symbol together; 'Safeguard' reads like a verb but supplies an electrical device.
explanation.definitionFit: The main structural shell of an aircraft, holding crew and passengers, is called this.

clue.text: Female thespian could be an influence

parts.note: a thespian is a stage performer

explanation.surface: A woman on stage might sway people.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an element contributing to an outcome, i.e. something that has an effect.

clue.text: Sun hell? —– may help

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday
Hades is the underworld of Greek myth

explanation.surface: Blazing sunshine feels like an inferno; something might ease it.
explanation.walkthrough: Sun here gives S for Sunday, while the whole clue describes sunglasses helping in fierce sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunglasses are informally called by this name and help when the sun is hellish.

clue.text: Get a load of tinsel tangled up

indicators.note: tangled up means knotted into disorder, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Look at this Christmas decoration all in a knot.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: 'get a load of this' is a slang call to pay attention or hear.

clue.text: I often hang around fruit

definitions.meaning: a third person who tags along awkwardly with a courting couple is said to play this role
a green, sour, hairy berry grown on a thorny bush

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an unwanted chaperone hanging round a couple and a tart green berry.

clue.text: Real quiet bloke with lasso?

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
a roper is a cowboy who catches cattle with a rope

explanation.surface: Asking whether a silent cowboy with his lariat is the genuine article.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something genuine or authentic, as in 'a real meal'.

clue.text: Practise on what moves late- comers, perhaps

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
the 'late' are the dead, and a funeral car carries them

explanation.surface: Drilling a routine about how to shift people who turn up late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' here means deceased, so late-comers are the dead arriving at a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to run through a performance in preparation.

clue.text: Spooner, say, with a beer outside gets the upper hand

indicators.note: outside says the beer word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: pils is a pale lager, short for pilsner
William Spooner was a clergyman, so he was a Reverend, REV

explanation.surface: The famous Oxford don, over a drink, comes out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooner' is not a Spoonerism signal here: it stands for a reverend.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: wins out or triumphs over opposition.

clue.text: Seedy district where waiting is a must

definitions.meaning: a disreputable area known for prostitution is called this kind of district
at a stop signal on the road, drivers must halt

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a sleazy area of town and a traffic signal ordering drivers to stop.

clue.text: Husband's tucked in so watch revamped programme?

indicators.note: tucked in says one letter is slipped inside the other letters
revamped means remade, so the letters of 'so watch' are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband, as in genealogy tables

explanation.surface: A domestic scene: the husband snug in bed, so the TV schedule is revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revamped' rearranges SO WATCH, and 'tucked in' places the extra H among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A television programme in which a host interviews guests is an example of a programme; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Knowing a thing or two animal finally scarpered

parts.note: a shrew is a small mouse-like mammal

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A savvy little creature that ran off at the last moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone who knows a thing or two is astute and sharp in judgement.

clue.text: Public looked attentive

parts.note: open means public, accessible to all
eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: The crowd watched closely.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: watchful and alert, with nothing escaping notice.

clue.text: From South Africa I will follow distant expedition

indicators.note: will follow says the letter I comes after the preceding piece

parts.note: far means distant

explanation.surface: A traveller from South Africa announcing a far-flung trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunting or viewing trip in Africa is a kind of journey or expedition.

clue.text: Restraints ruined one from a group of sellers

definitions.text: one from a group of sellers

parts.note: chains are shackles or restraints
tore means ripped or damaged

explanation.surface: Broken shackles freeing one member of a band of traders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' looks like an anagram signal but supplies a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop belonging to a group under one owner is one outlet of that retailer.

clue.text: He must heal sick old man with bottle

indicators.note: sick suggests something disordered, so the three words before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor's duty to cure an ailing pensioner who has a drink problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on two senses: the very long-lived biblical patriarch, and a large wine bottle named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical figure lived 969 years, the archetypal old man, and his name is used for a champagne bottle holding eight standard bottles.

clue.text: We do short messages — time with little rest breaks

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

indicators.note: breaks means smashed apart, so the letters of the following word are scrambled

explanation.surface: Busy people texting briefly during short rest breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Users of social media who post brief updates describe themselves in this way.

clue.text: She cleans heads with habitual response

parts.note: domes is slang for heads
a tic is an involuntary habitual twitch

explanation.surface: A cleaner whose heads twitch in habitual reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: A household servant who does housework is a cleaner.

clue.text: Bill, eg, slipped into calm romantic song

indicators.note: slipped into says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: serene means calm
a bill (poster) is an example of an advertisement, AD

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill drifting into a tranquil love song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name; it is a poster, an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A love song sung beneath a sweetheart's window, a romantic tune.

clue.text: Good bread (so some say) while argon welding

indicators.note: welding fuses pieces into a new form, so the letters of the two words are recombined

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A health claim about loaves set beside a workshop scene of gas-shielded welding.
explanation.walkthrough: '(so some say)' hedges 'Good': the loaf is reputed healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread made with the entire kernel is widely promoted as healthier, so some call it good bread.

clue.text: Steamship stuck in strong struggle

indicators.note: stuck in says one piece is lodged inside another

parts.note: hale means healthy and strong

explanation.surface: A steamer stuck fast in a powerful fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: effort and bother, as in a fight to get something done.

clue.text: Season what's first set to rest?

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: to inter is to bury, laying the dead to rest

explanation.surface: Asking which time of year comes first to lay things down.
explanation.definitionFit: The coldest quarter of the year is one of the four seasons.

clue.text: This may trickle right through mist, possibly

indicators.note: through says one letter runs inside the other word

parts.note: steam is a kind of mist or vapour

explanation.surface: Something dripping straight through fog.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brook or flow of water can trickle along.

clue.text: Team found inside motel eventually

indicators.note: found inside says the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A sports side tracked down at a motel at last.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has this many players, so the number stands for the team.

clue.text: Space? It's prepared for one mad on getting away

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or worked up, so the letters are reorganised

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; the apostrophe is ignored

explanation.surface: Room has been readied for someone desperate for a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who seeks distraction from reality, keen on flight from routine.

clue.text: We make a crowd? Divorcees grabbing pictures, say, back

indicators.note: grabbing says the outer word seizes and holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: exs (also spelt exes) are former spouses

indicators.note: back says the word for pictures is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: art is exemplified by pictures

explanation.surface: Former spouses snatching photos, wondering if they count as a mob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word for pictures and 'grabbing' puts it within the former partners; the question mark warns that 'We make a crowd' is a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Film background performers who fill out crowd scenes are hired in numbers to form a crowd.

clue.text: Little hubbub in Paris, I imagine, for lamb cut

definitions.text: Little hubbub in Paris, I imagine
definitions.meaning: playfully read as a small din dressed up with the French diminutive ending -ette
a small round boneless piece of meat, such as from a loin of lamb

explanation.surface: A French chef's small fuss over a joint of lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is whimsical: the setter imagines a French diminutive of a word for din.
explanation.definitionFit: Butchers use the French term for a small round medallion of lamb loin.

clue.text: Pack an ostentatious way of going, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is said out loud and a like-sounding word is entered

parts.note: to sashay is to walk in a showy, swaggering way

explanation.surface: Showing off with a flamboyant strut while packing.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sealed packet, as of sugar or shampoo, is a little pack.

clue.text: Doctor met with large message

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A physician met someone carrying a big communication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person but is a verb meaning alter.
explanation.definitionFit: A wired communication delivered on paper is a kind of message.
